guitar.evidence: Alvin Lee's heavily modified, stickered Gibson ES-335 nicknamed 'Big Red' is one of the most iconic and well-documented guitars in rock history, famously played at Woodstock on 'I'm Going Home'.

tone.target: hot, biting British blues-rock lead with fast sustain and raw overdrive
tone.profile: hot, biting British blues-rock lead with fast sustain and raw overdrive
tone.summary: A high-gain, mid-focused chain using a Plexi-style amp model paired with an OD boost for aggressive lead tone, finished with room ambience.

rig.name: Alvin Lee & Ten Years After - I'm Going Home - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and excessive noise inherent in high-gain blues tones.
Provide aggressive lead bite and sustain boost without sounding like heavy fuzz.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate a mid-humped, biting overdrive characteristic of Plexi/Marshall tones.

alternatives.reason: Slightly warmer, but still effective for blues lead.

blocks.purpose: Add raw overdrive and grit to the core tone, simulating tube saturation.
blocks.gap: Used as a secondary gain stage to push the amp into aggressive territory, mimicking classic British rock drive.

alternatives.reason: More general distortion; RAT-style offers more bite.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the aggressive, mid-focused sound of a Marshall Plexi/British blues amp.
blocks.gap: The UK SLP model is chosen for its classic British voicing and ability to achieve high gain without excessive modern sheen.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative, but the SLP often provides a more aggressive lead tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British rock cabinet voicing and necessary high-end punch.
Boost the upper mids and highs to achieve 'biting' lead bite and cut through the mix.
blocks.gap: Used to manually sculpt the frequency response, emphasizing the mid-range punch required for blues leads.

alternatives.reason: Similar function, but EQ 2 allows for more precise high/mid boosts.

blocks.purpose: Subtle thickening and movement for lead lines (optional). Kept low to avoid sounding 'modern sheen'.
blocks.gap: The Chorus is used subtly, primarily as a texture enhancer rather than a core tone element.

blocks.purpose: Add a slight sense of space and depth without washing out the raw tone.
blocks.gap: The 'slight room' requirement is met by using a moderate mix Room reverb.

alternatives.reason: Can be too bright or artificial for this specific blues-rock tone.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet simulation to provide more aggressive, biting high-end response suitable for classic blues lead tones.

proposals.reason: Enhance upper mids and bite for aggressive blues lead.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and punch in the high end.
